sections.title: Databricks Intelligence Platform
objectives: Enable features that simplify data layout decisions and optimize query performance
Explain the value of the Data Intelligence Platform
Identify the applicable compute to use for a specific use case
sections.notes:
The value of the Data Intelligence Platform

One platform over a single lakehouse (open Delta/Parquet in cloud storage) that unifies engineering, analytics, ML and AI, governed end-to-end by Unity Catalog. "Intelligence" = AI woven in (assistant, natural-language search, predictive optimization). Key wins: open formats (no lock-in), one governance layer, collaboration, ACID via Delta Lake.

Optimizing data layout & query performance

  • Delta Lake gives ACID transactions, time travel, schema enforcement.
  • Liquid Clustering — modern replacement for partitioning + ZORDER; cluster a table on chosen keys, Databricks manages layout as data grows.
  • Predictive Optimization — Databricks auto-runs OPTIMIZE (compaction) and VACUUM for you.
  • Legacy levers you should still recognize: OPTIMIZE (compact small files), ZORDER BY (co-locate by column), partitioning, auto compaction.

Pick the right compute

  • All-purpose compute — interactive notebook/dev work; can be shared; stays up.
  • Job compute — spun up for an automated job and torn down after; cheaper for scheduled work.
  • SQL warehouse — for SQL/BI queries and dashboards.
  • Serverless vs classic — serverless starts fast and is managed/auto-optimized by Databricks; classic runs in your cloud account.

Rule of thumb: scheduled pipeline → job compute (or serverless); a person exploring in a notebook → all-purpose; BI/SQL dashboard → SQL warehouse.

Compute types: all-purpose vs jobs vs SQL warehouse

quiz.q: A scheduled nightly ETL job currently runs on an always-on all-purpose cluster. The team wants to cut cost without changing the logic. What's the best change?
opts: Switch the job to a SQL warehouse
Run it on job compute that starts and terminates with the run
Move the job to a personal cluster
quiz.e: Job compute is provisioned for the run and torn down after, so you don't pay for idle time. SQL warehouses are for SQL/BI, not arbitrary ETL logic.

quiz.q: Which feature lets Databricks automatically run OPTIMIZE and VACUUM on a table so engineers don't have to schedule them?
quiz.e: Predictive Optimization automates maintenance like compaction (OPTIMIZE) and cleanup (VACUUM).

quiz.q: A team wants to cluster a large Delta table on frequently filtered columns and have Databricks manage the layout as it grows, instead of choosing partitions and ZORDER manually. What should they use?
quiz.e: Liquid Clustering replaces the old partition + ZORDER approach and adapts the layout automatically.

quiz.q: Which is a core value of the Data Intelligence Platform / lakehouse architecture?
opts: It stores data in a proprietary closed format for speed
It unifies engineering, BI and AI on open formats with one governance layer
It requires a separate data warehouse and data lake
It removes the need for any compute
quiz.obj: Explain the value of the platform
quiz.e: The lakehouse unifies workloads on open formats (Delta/Parquet) governed by Unity Catalog — no separate warehouse + lake silos.

quiz.q: Which compute is the right default for a BI dashboard issuing SQL queries?
quiz.e: SQL warehouses are purpose-built for SQL and BI tools.

quiz.q: Which Delta Lake capability lets you query a previous version of a table (e.g. as of a past timestamp)?
quiz.e: Delta Lake keeps a transaction log, enabling time travel to earlier versions of a table.

quiz.q: The lakehouse stores data in which open formats?
opts: An in-memory format that isn't persisted
quiz.obj: Explain the value of the platform
quiz.e: The lakehouse uses open Delta/Parquet files in cloud storage — no proprietary lock-in.

quiz.q: What does the OPTIMIZE command do to a Delta table?
opts: Compacts many small files into fewer larger ones
quiz.e: OPTIMIZE compacts small files to improve read performance; VACUUM is the separate cleanup command.

quiz.q: Compared to classic compute, serverless compute is best described as:
opts: Running in your own cloud account and manually tuned
Managed and auto-optimized by Databricks with fast startup
quiz.e: Serverless is managed and auto-optimized by Databricks and starts quickly; classic runs in your cloud account.

flashcards.back: One platform over open Delta/Parquet files in cloud storage that unifies engineering, analytics, ML and AI — no separate warehouse + lake silos.
The single governance layer that governs the platform end-to-end (data, AI assets, permissions, lineage).
Storage layer giving ACID transactions, time travel, and schema enforcement on top of Parquet.
Modern replacement for partitioning + ZORDER: you pick cluster keys and Databricks manages the data layout automatically as the table grows.
Databricks automatically runs maintenance like OPTIMIZE (compaction) and VACUUM (cleanup) so engineers don't have to schedule them.
Legacy layout levers: OPTIMIZE compacts small files; ZORDER BY co-locates data by column. Liquid Clustering now supersedes this combo.
Interactive notebook/dev work; can be shared and stays up. Best for a person exploring.
Spun up for an automated job and torn down after it finishes — cheaper for scheduled work (no idle cost).
Compute purpose-built for SQL/BI queries and dashboards.
Serverless starts fast and is managed/auto-optimized by Databricks; classic runs in your own cloud account.

sections.title: Development & Ingestion
sections.weightHint: Notebooks, Auto Loader, Databricks Connect, debugging
objectives: Use Databricks Connect in a data engineering workflow
Determine the capabilities of Notebooks functionality
Classify valid Auto Loader sources and use cases
Demonstrate knowledge of Auto Loader syntax
Use Databricks' built-in debugging tools to troubleshoot a given issue
sections.notes:
Databricks Connect

Run code from your local IDE (VS Code, PyCharm) or app against remote Databricks compute. You develop locally with full PySpark/Spark Connect but execution happens on the cluster — handy for testing and apps without working only in the web notebook.

Notebooks

  • Multi-language cells via magics: %python, %sql, %scala, %r, %md, %sh.
  • %run ./other_notebook imports another notebook; dbutils for files, secrets, widgets; dbutils.widgets for parameters.
  • Collaborative editing, version history, results, and visualizations inline.

Auto Loader (incremental file ingestion)

  • Incrementally and efficiently loads new files as they land in cloud object storage (S3, ADLS, GCS).
  • Uses the cloudFiles source, tracks what's processed via a checkpoint, and supports schema inference & evolution.
  • Best for: continuously / unpredictably arriving files; far better than re-listing a whole directory each run.
spark.readStream
  .format("cloudFiles")
  .option("cloudFiles.format", "json")
  .option("cloudFiles.schemaLocation", "/chk/schema")
  .load("/landing/events")
.writeStream
  .option("checkpointLocation", "/chk/events")
  .table("bronze_events")

Debugging tools

  • Spark UI — see stages/tasks, find skew, shuffle, and spills.
  • Notebook error tracebacks; df.explain() for the query plan; cluster event logs and driver/executor logs.
videos: Databricks notebook magic commands dbutils widgets tutorial

quiz.q: Which source format string does Auto Loader use in spark.readStream.format(...) ?
quiz.e: Auto Loader is invoked with format("cloudFiles") and the underlying file type set via the cloudFiles.format option.

quiz.q: Which scenario is the best fit for Auto Loader?
opts: A one-time load of a single static CSV
Continuously ingesting new JSON files that land in a cloud storage folder
Querying a Delta table for a dashboard
Sharing a table with an external partner
quiz.e: Auto Loader shines for incrementally picking up new files as they arrive in cloud object storage.

quiz.q: A data engineer wants to develop and test PySpark code in VS Code but execute it on a Databricks cluster. What should they use?
quiz.e: Databricks Connect runs locally-authored code against remote Databricks compute.

quiz.q: In a Databricks notebook, which command runs another notebook inline so its functions/variables are available?
quiz.e: %run ./notebook executes another notebook in the same context.

quiz.q: A streaming Auto Loader job must avoid reprocessing files it already ingested after a restart. What makes this work?
quiz.e: The checkpoint tracks processed files and stream progress, so a restart resumes without duplicating work.

quiz.q: Which built-in tool best helps diagnose a slow stage caused by data skew?
quiz.e: The Spark UI exposes stages/tasks, shuffle and skew so you can pinpoint the bottleneck.

quiz.q: Which notebook magic command renders a cell as formatted markdown text?
quiz.e: %md renders markdown; %sh runs shell, %sql runs SQL, %run executes another notebook.

quiz.q: Auto Loader needs to infer and track a table's schema over time. Which option points it at the schema store?
quiz.e: cloudFiles.schemaLocation stores the inferred schema and supports schema evolution.

quiz.q: Which utility parameterizes a notebook so a job can pass in values?
quiz.e: dbutils.widgets defines notebook parameters/widgets that can be set at runtime.

quiz.q: To inspect how Spark will execute a DataFrame query (its plan), you use:
quiz.e: df.explain() prints the physical/logical query plan, useful for debugging performance.

flashcards.back: Run locally-authored code (VS Code, PyCharm) against remote Databricks compute — develop locally, execute on the cluster.
%python, %sql, %scala, %r, %md, %sh let a single notebook mix languages cell by cell.
%run ./other_notebook executes another notebook inline so its functions/variables are available in the current context.
Notebook utilities for files, secrets, and widgets; dbutils.widgets defines parameters.
Incrementally and efficiently loads only NEW files as they land in cloud object storage (S3, ADLS, GCS).
The source format string Auto Loader uses: spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles"), with the file type set via cloudFiles.format.
Tracks which files/offsets a stream has processed so a restart resumes without reprocessing or duplicating work.
Auto Loader can infer the schema and adapt as new columns appear, using a schema location.
Built-in tool showing stages/tasks, shuffle, skew and spills — used to find performance bottlenecks.
Prints the query plan to help debug and understand how Spark will execute a DataFrame.

sections.title: Data Processing & Transformations
objectives: Describe the three layers of the Medallion Architecture and the purpose of each
Classify the cluster type/configuration for optimal performance by scenario
Explain the advantages of LDP (Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines) for ETL
Implement data pipelines using LDP
Identify DDL/DML features
Compute complex aggregations and metrics with PySpark DataFrames
sections.notes:
Medallion architecture

  • Bronze — raw, as-ingested data (append-only landing zone, keeps history/fidelity).
  • Silver — cleaned, filtered, conformed, joined; the trustworthy "enterprise" view.
  • Gold — business-level aggregates/marts ready for BI, ML, reporting.

Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines (LDP, formerly Delta Live Tables)

  • You declare the tables and their transformations; Databricks handles orchestration, dependencies, retries, and scaling.
  • Built-in data quality expectations (EXPECT) to drop/quarantine bad rows.
  • Supports streaming tables (incremental) and materialized views.
-- SQL form
CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE bronze
AS SELECT * FROM cloud_files('/landing','json');

CREATE OR REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW silver
( CONSTRAINT valid_id EXPECT (id IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW )
AS SELECT * FROM bronze WHERE amount > 0;

DDL / DML you must know

  • DDL: CREATE TABLE, CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE (always overwrites), CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS (only if absent), ALTER, DROP, CTAS (CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT).
  • DML: INSERT INTO, UPDATE, DELETE, and MERGE INTO (upserts).

PySpark aggregations

  • df.groupBy("col").agg(...) with sum, avg, count, and count_distinct (unique counts).
  • count("x") counts rows; count_distinct("x") counts unique values — pick carefully (e.g., unique invoices).
videos: Databricks medallion architecture bronze silver gold explained
Delta Live Tables / Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines
Databricks Delta Live Tables tutorial expectations streaming table

quiz.q: Which statement best describes the SILVER layer?
opts: Raw, untouched data exactly as ingested
Cleaned, conformed, validated data joined into a trustworthy view
quiz.e: Bronze = raw, Silver = cleaned/conformed, Gold = business aggregates.

quiz.q: You need a SQL DDL statement that creates a Delta table, overwriting any existing table of the same name. Which is correct?
opts: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS t (...)
quiz.e: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE recreates the table regardless of whether it already exists. IF NOT EXISTS does the opposite.

quiz.q: Which PySpark snippet returns total amount and the count of UNIQUE invoice ids per day?
quiz.e: count_distinct('inv_id') gives unique invoices; count() would include duplicates and sum() on an id is meaningless.

quiz.q: A key advantage of Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines (LDP) over hand-written notebook ETL is:
opts: It declares tables and auto-manages orchestration, quality, and scaling
quiz.e: LDP is declarative: you define the tables/transforms and it handles orchestration, retries, data-quality expectations, and scaling.

quiz.q: Which clause in LDP drops rows that fail a data-quality rule?
quiz.e: LDP expectations (EXPECT) define quality constraints; ON VIOLATION DROP ROW removes bad records.

quiz.q: To upsert (insert new, update existing) rows into a Delta table, which DML command is designed for the job?
quiz.e: MERGE INTO performs conditional insert/update/delete — the standard upsert pattern.

quiz.q: In the medallion architecture, which layer holds raw, as-ingested data kept for history and fidelity?
quiz.e: Bronze is the raw append-only landing layer; Silver is cleaned/conformed; Gold is business aggregates.

quiz.q: In Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines, which object incrementally ingests new data as it arrives?
quiz.e: Streaming tables process data incrementally; materialized views recompute results from their sources.

quiz.q: What does the DDL statement CREATE TABLE sales AS SELECT * FROM staging (CTAS) do?
opts: Creates a new table populated from a query
Deletes rows that fail a constraint
quiz.e: CTAS (CREATE TABLE AS SELECT) creates and populates a new table from a query's results.

quiz.q: Which PySpark expression returns the average order value per customer?
quiz.e: groupBy('cust').agg(avg('amount')) computes the mean amount within each customer group.

flashcards.back: Raw, as-ingested data — an append-only landing zone that keeps full history and fidelity.
Cleaned, filtered, conformed and joined data — the trustworthy enterprise view.
Business-level aggregates/marts ready for BI, ML and reporting.
Formerly Delta Live Tables: you declare tables and transforms; Databricks handles orchestration, dependencies, retries and scaling.
LDP data-quality constraints; e.g. EXPECT (id IS NOT NULL) ON VIOLATION DROP ROW drops or quarantines bad rows.
LDP supports streaming tables (incremental) and materialized views (recomputed results).
DDL that always (re)creates the table, overwriting any existing one of the same name.
DDL that creates the table only if it does not already exist (the opposite of OR REPLACE).
DML for upserts — conditional insert/update/delete in one statement.
count("x") counts rows; count_distinct("x") counts unique values (e.g. unique invoices) — choose carefully.

sections.title: Productionizing Data Pipelines
sections.weightHint: Asset Bundles, Jobs, serverless, Spark UI
objectives: Identify the difference between DAB and traditional deployment methods
Identify the structure of Asset Bundles
Deploy a workflow; repair and rerun a task after failure
Use serverless for hands-off, auto-optimized compute
Analyze the Spark UI to optimize a query
sections.notes:
Databricks Asset Bundles (DAB)

  • Infrastructure-as-code for Databricks: define jobs, pipelines, and settings in YAML and deploy with the Databricks CLI (databricks bundle deploy).
  • Vs traditional (clicking in the UI / ad-hoc): bundles are version-controlled, repeatable, and promotable across environments (dev → staging → prod) via targets.
  • Structure: a databricks.yml at the root with resources (jobs, pipelines) and targets (per-environment overrides), plus your source files.
bundle:
  name: sales_pipeline
resources:
  jobs:
    nightly_etl:
      tasks: [ ... ]
targets:
  dev: { mode: development }
  prod: { mode: production }

Jobs / Workflows

  • A job has one or more tasks with dependencies, schedules, and retries.
  • On failure you can Repair run — rerun only the failed task(s) instead of the whole job.

Serverless

Hands-off, auto-optimized compute managed by Databricks — fast startup, no cluster sizing/tuning. Good default for jobs and pipelines when you don't want to manage clusters.

Spark UI for optimization

  • Look for skew (one task far slower), heavy shuffle, and spill to disk (not enough memory).
  • Stages/tasks timeline shows where time goes; fix with better partitioning, broadcast joins, or caching.
videos: Databricks Asset Bundles tutorial databricks.yml deploy
Jobs / Workflows: tasks, schedule, repair run
Databricks Workflows jobs repair run failed task tutorial
Reading the Spark UI to find skew & shuffle
Databricks Spark UI tutorial skew shuffle spill

quiz.q: A failed multi-task job needs only the one broken task re-executed, keeping successful tasks' results. What do you use?
quiz.e: Repair run reruns just the failed task(s) rather than the entire job.

quiz.q: What's the main advantage of Databricks Asset Bundles over deploying by clicking in the UI?
opts: They run faster at query time
They make deployments version-controlled, repeatable, and promotable across environments
They remove the need for compute
quiz.e: DABs are IaC: defined in YAML, source-controlled, and deployable across dev/prod targets consistently.

quiz.q: In an Asset Bundle, where are per-environment settings like dev vs prod defined?
quiz.e: targets hold environment-specific configuration; resources define jobs/pipelines.

quiz.q: A team wants job compute with fast startup and no cluster sizing or tuning. Best choice?
quiz.e: Serverless is hands-off and auto-optimized by Databricks, with fast startup.

quiz.q: In the Spark UI, one task in a stage takes 10× longer than the others. This most likely indicates:
quiz.e: A single very slow task among many usually means skew — uneven data distribution across partitions.

quiz.q: Which Databricks CLI command deploys the jobs/pipelines defined in a bundle?
quiz.e: `databricks bundle deploy` deploys the resources defined in databricks.yml to the target environment.

quiz.q: In the Spark UI, 'spill' (memory to disk) during a stage usually indicates:
opts: Not enough memory, so data is written to disk
quiz.e: Spill means tasks ran out of memory and had to write to disk, which slows the job.

quiz.q: A Databricks job (workflow) is composed of:
opts: One or more tasks with dependencies, schedules, and retries
quiz.e: A job orchestrates one or more tasks with dependencies, scheduling, and retry behavior.

quiz.q: Which files does a Databricks Asset Bundle use to define its configuration?
quiz.e: Bundles are defined in YAML (databricks.yml) with resources and targets — infrastructure as code.

flashcards.back: Infrastructure-as-code for Databricks: define jobs, pipelines and settings in YAML and deploy with the Databricks CLI.
Bundles are version-controlled, repeatable and promotable across environments (dev → staging → prod); clicking in the UI is ad-hoc and not reproducible.
Root bundle file holding resources (jobs, pipelines) and targets (per-environment overrides).
The DAB section that holds environment-specific configuration like dev vs prod.
The DAB section that defines jobs and pipelines.
Reruns only the failed task(s) of a job, keeping the results of tasks that already succeeded.
Hands-off, auto-optimized compute with fast startup and no cluster sizing/tuning — a good default for jobs/pipelines.
One task in a stage takes far longer than the others — a sign of uneven data distribution across partitions.
Heavy shuffle moves data across the cluster; spill is writing to disk when memory runs out — both hurt performance.

sections.title: Data Governance & Quality
sections.weightHint: Unity Catalog, grants, lineage, Delta Sharing, Federation
objectives: Explain the difference between managed and external tables
Identify how to grant permissions to users and groups within UC
Identify key roles in UC
Identify how audit logs are stored
Use lineage features in Unity Catalog
Use Delta Sharing to share data; know its advantages and limitations
Identify types of Delta Sharing (Databricks-to-Databricks vs external)
Analyze cost considerations of sharing across clouds
Identify use cases of Lakehouse Federation
sections.notes:
Managed vs external tables

  • Managed — Unity Catalog manages both metadata and the underlying data files. DROP deletes the data.
  • External — data lives in an external location you specify; UC manages only metadata. DROP keeps the data files.

Unity Catalog namespace & grants

  • Three levels: catalog.schema.table. To read a table a user typically needs USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA, and SELECT.
  • GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA sales TO analysts; — read-only. MODIFY for write; ALL PRIVILEGES for everything.
  • Roles: metastore admin, account admin, plus object owners who can grant on what they own.

Lineage & audit

  • UC captures lineage automatically — table/column-level, upstream/downstream, including notebooks and dashboards.
  • Audit logs are delivered/stored to a cloud storage location (and queryable system tables) for who-did-what.

Delta Sharing

  • Open protocol to share live data without copying it. Two flavors: Databricks-to-Databricks (recipient is on Databricks) and open sharing to external non-Databricks clients.
  • You create a share, add tables/views, and grant recipients read access.
  • Watch cross-cloud egress cost when the recipient is in a different cloud/region.

Lakehouse Federation

Query external systems (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, Redshift, etc.) in place from Databricks without ingesting the data first — great for exploration and joining external sources under UC governance.

Databricks Unity Catalog managed vs external tables grants tutorial
Databricks Delta Sharing tutorial databricks to databricks external

quiz.q: You DROP a Unity Catalog table and the underlying data files remain in cloud storage. The table was:
quiz.e: External tables keep their data on DROP (UC manages only metadata). Dropping a managed table deletes the data.

quiz.q: An analyst group already has USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA on sales_data and needs read-only access. Which grant is correct?
opts: GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON SCHEMA sales_data TO analysts
GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA sales_data TO analysts
GRANT INSERT ON SCHEMA sales_data TO analysts
GRANT MODIFY ON SCHEMA sales_data TO analysts
quiz.e: SELECT gives read-only access. ALL PRIVILEGES/INSERT/MODIFY grant write capability.

quiz.q: A partner who does NOT use Databricks needs to read a shared dataset. Which applies?
quiz.e: Open Delta Sharing serves recipients on non-Databricks/external clients; D2D is for recipients already on Databricks.

quiz.q: A team wants to query a Snowflake table from Databricks without first copying the data in. Best fit?
quiz.e: Lakehouse Federation queries external sources in place under UC governance.

quiz.q: Which is an accurate cost consideration for Delta Sharing across clouds?
opts: Sharing is always free regardless of location
Cross-cloud / cross-region data egress can incur cost
Recipients must duplicate the data to read it
quiz.e: Reading shared data across clouds/regions can trigger egress charges — plan placement accordingly.

quiz.q: Where does Unity Catalog get table- and column-level lineage from?
opts: It's captured automatically as queries run
quiz.e: UC captures lineage automatically across notebooks, jobs, and dashboards.

quiz.q: A Unity Catalog object is referenced with how many namespace levels?
quiz.e: UC uses a three-level namespace: catalog.schema.table.

quiz.q: Besides SELECT on the table, what does a user typically also need to read a table in Unity Catalog?
quiz.e: Reading a table generally requires USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA plus SELECT on the table.

quiz.q: A key advantage of Delta Sharing is that it shares live data:
quiz.e: Delta Sharing is an open protocol that shares live data without copying it (to Databricks or external clients).

quiz.q: You DROP a managed Unity Catalog table. What happens to the underlying data files?
opts: They convert to an external table
quiz.e: For a managed table, UC manages the data, so DROP deletes the underlying files (unlike an external table).

flashcards.back: Unity Catalog manages both the metadata and the underlying data files — DROP deletes the data.
Data lives in an external location you specify; UC manages only metadata — DROP keeps the data files.
Three levels: catalog.schema.table. Reading a table typically needs USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and SELECT.
Gives read-only access to an object; MODIFY adds write, ALL PRIVILEGES grants everything.
Metastore admin, account admin, plus object owners who can grant privileges on what they own.
UC captures table- and column-level lineage automatically as queries run, across notebooks, jobs and dashboards.
Recorded who-did-what, delivered to a cloud storage location and queryable via system tables.
Open protocol to share live data without copying it.
Databricks-to-Databricks sharing (recipient on Databricks) vs open sharing to external, non-Databricks clients.
Reading shared data across clouds/regions can incur data egress cost — plan placement.
Query external systems (PostgreSQL, MySQL, Snowflake, Redshift…) in place from Databricks, under UC governance, without ingesting first.
